newsitem.title: USA: Conseco to buy Colonial Penn for $460 mln.
newsitem.headline: Conseco to buy Colonial Penn for $460 mln.

text.p: Conseco Inc said Wednesday it agreed to acquire the Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co unit of Leucadia National Corp for $460 million in cash and notes.
The transaction is subject to customary terms and conditions, including regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the third quarter of 1997, Conseco said.
Conseco said the transaction is expected to be modestly accretive to its operating earnings per share.

Colonial Penn uses direct response marketing to sell graded benefit life insurance, a level-premium whole life product designed to meet the needs of seniors who have little or no other life protection, Conseco said.

Direct response marketing includes the use of television advertising, direct mail and telemarketing to generate sales leads. Colonial Penn maintains a database of more than 15 million policyholders and prospects, Conseco said.

Conseco chairman Stephen Hilbert said the transaction "adds an important distribution channel and represents an important strategic step toward our goal of developing the finest product delivery capability in the industry.
He said Colonial Penn presents Conseco with the opportunity to expand its reach into the senior marketplace and to cross-market other Conseco products using Colonial Penn's direct marketing arm.
"The ability to efficiently distribute products, we are convinced, will be the defining characteristic of tomorrow's industry leaders," he said.

He said Conseco's strategic objective is to become the nation's premier provider of insurance products to the age 40-plus consumer by strengthening its position in each of its major product lines: supplemental health insurance, annuities, and life insurance.
